observations.text: i18n/style-guides/fr.md renders its plural example with '#' (grouped '1 000 000') and its Numbers rule calls for grouped digits, while all nine arms use the explicit {count, number, ::group-off} skeleton. Ungrouped digits are what the repo's own guard enforces — scripts/i18n/chat-data-copy.test.mjs (changed in this same PR) asserts out.includes("1000000") and rejects any digit grouping — so '1 000 000 d’agents' would fail the shipped guard. The arm correctly copies the English skeleton; the guide's example is the outlying text. Untouched by this delta, not a finding on it.

At count 0 {list} is empty, so the =0 arm reads '… — . Vous pourrez les modifier…'. Identical in English, unchanged by this delta, and unreachable because chat-sidebar.tsx gates the sentence on availableBuiltins.length > 0.

count = names.length of the backend's available built-ins (builtin-offer-sentence.ts), and the spelling arms cover 0–6. A 1,000,000-profile backend does not exist, so the new `many` arm is CLDR completeness rather than a rendered state: this change has no user-visible frame to screenshot. Correct and consistent with the namespace's other many-bearing keys; the manager should treat the PR's user-visible claim accordingly.
